exceptions.justification: The runtime suite's end-to-end baseline is a plain async function that returns a pre-built array and spreads it into an object, with no data-cap code. Its true cost is constant and sub-microsecond, so its fitted exponent (0.01 at the last release, 0.37 and 0.42 on two runs of this pull request) is timer noise on a different CPU model (EPYC 9V45 against the reference EPYC 7763), not a change in the package.
exceptions.ruleBroken: A benchmark group must not get worse at big-O than at the last release without a human accepting it.
exceptions.attempted: Re-ran the failed job once (exponent 0.42, same flip). Compared the baseline's code against the last release: no source in data-cap is on its path.
exceptions.constraint: The reference results were measured on another CPU model and the baseline is too fast for the growth fit to be stable; the measurement cannot be made stable from inside this repository.
exceptions.whyPreferable: Accepting a named, expiring record for one group that runs no package code is preferable to widening the gate for every group or turning off the complexity-gain check.
exceptions.residualRisk: A real regression in the baseline cannot exist because it runs no data-cap code. The with-package group, which does, stays judged on its own growth class and on the overhead ratio.
exceptions.revisitWhen: The next release records new reference results on the CI runner's CPU model, or internal-package-contract stops judging groups whose fit is not trusted.
